name: SqueezeLLM: Dense-and-Sparse Quantization
authors: Kim, Joo, Kim, Liu, James, Burger, Akoglu
problem: Single-batch generative LLM inference is memory-bandwidth-bound, so weights must shrink - but uniform low-bit quantization loses perplexity badly at 3 bits.
mechanism: Two components: (1) sensitivity-based NON-UNIFORM quantization - per-row bit precision allocation searched from second-order (Fisher-style) sensitivity information so sensitive rows get more bits; (2) the Dense-and-Sparse decomposition - outlier and sensitive weight values are stored in a sparse residual format while the bulk is stored as dense low-bit codebooks, cutting both bytes and dequantization work.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract, LLaMA family): lossless (to their definition) compression at up to 3 bits, and at 3-bit the perplexity gap from the FP16 baseline is reduced 'by up to 2.1x' versus state-of-the-art methods at the same memory budget. COMPRESSION RATIO: up to ~5.3x at 3 bits vs FP16. QUALITY COST: 'lossless' is the paper's own wording at their threshold; the concrete number to trust is the 2.1x reduction in the perplexity gap. The paper's framing that inference is bandwidth- not compute-bound for batch size 1 is the load-bearing insight and it generalizes beyond this method.
